answer: An agent market serving ridge surveys, falcon tracking, and kernel tuning requires each active identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before it can submit bids. Each identity gets one bidding slot, so an attacker seeking 1,000 slots must immobilize $100,000 for a month. Generating names or keys is cheap, but generating usable identities ties up capital and sacrifices interest or other investment returns, making a flood costly.
